## Runtime of `shared_importance()` (experiment D)

Timed: the shared_importance() call only (elapsed wall-clock time); reading the data, building the fold list, process and container start-up are outside the timed region. 1 warm-up run (discarded) and 5 timed runs per cell, 1 thread; one process per language and learner; the processes run one after the other, nothing else is run by the workflow at the same time; within a process the cells are run in increasing order of predicted time. Data: x1 ~ N(0, 1), x_j = 0.5 x_{j-1} + sqrt(0.75) e_j (unit variances, correlation 0.5^|j-k|); y = 2 x1 + x2 - x3 + 0.5 x4 x5 + N(0, 1); values rounded to 6 decimals; metric mse; the same file and fold column in both languages. Sweeps: one factor at a time around the base cell: the n sweep at p = 10, v = 5; the p sweep at n = 1000, v = 5; the v sweep at n = 1000, p = 10. One call fits the learner 2 x p x v times (`learner_fits`).

Seconds are wall-clock seconds; `q1`, `q3` are the quartiles of the timed runs (IQR = q3 - q1). Differences between R and Python include the learner implementations, the linear-algebra libraries and the overhead of each framework; they are not differences "between the languages".

## Budget

A cell costs (warmup_runs + timed_runs) x predicted seconds. A cell whose cost exceeds the per-cell cap is not run and is recorded as 'skipped (budget)'. The cap is the largest candidate for which the cost of all remaining cells of all processes plus the process overheads is at most planned_fraction x total_seconds. If the warm-up run of a cell shows that the cell would cost more than abort_factor x the cap, the cell is stopped and recorded as 'skipped (budget, after warm-up)'. If a process has used more than 1.25 x its planned time, its remaining cells are recorded as 'skipped (budget, process allowance)'.
